Subject: Marketplace PO: unit price mapping & target $/1M — follow-up

Hi Tina / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can move toward a private offer (PO) that maps cleanly to the unit economics the Nimbus team needs.

Recap (from our side):
- Nimbus is evaluating an initial 6–12 month commitment for generative inference: expected monthly consumption ~250M–450M input+output tokens (peaks vary by campaign).
- Target economics (Nimbus): target net spend to vendor of ~$30–$45 per 1M tokens. They expect the marketplace gross to be higher to cover distributor/marketplace fees.
- Ask: confirm whether AWS Marketplace requires us to publish the gross unit price (i.e., the buyer-facing per-1M price) and whether the marketplace fee is taken on top or as a revenue share out of the gross.

Concrete items we need from AWS to align mapping:
1) Marketplace fee % or routing (typical guidance we saw on the call was ~20% but we need final confirmation).
2) Whether PO line items support per-1M token unit granularity vs. per-1000 tokens.
3) Any constraints on rounding or minimum price increments in the PO console.

From Redwood: we attached a simple pricing scenario workbook (pricing-scenario-0615.xlsx) with three mapping options (net target -> required gross on marketplace at 15/20/25% fees). If AWS confirms fee rules and rounding, we can produce a PO draft with line-item unit prices that map to Nimbus’s target net $/1M.

Next steps proposed:
- Tina: confirm marketplace fee % and rounding rules + any docs we should include in the PO.
- Sam (Nimbus): confirm the expected monthly commit band (250–450M is our current estimate) and whether they need a progressive tiered unit price.
- Redwood (us): produce a PO draft and an example gross->net mapping for 3 fee scenarios; legal/finance review window ~48–72h after we hand off the draft.

Thanks — attaching the scenario workbook for review.

Best,

Subject: Re: Marketplace PO: unit price mapping & target $/1M — follow-up

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. A few quick clarifications from AWS Marketplace side: 

- Marketplace model: Private Offers support custom unit pricing set on the offer line item. The buyer-facing price is the gross unit price. AWS collects the gross from the buyer and then remits payment to the seller net of the Marketplace fee.
- Fee %: Standard fee is 20% for Marketplace listing revenue share unless a partner discount/waiver has been negotiated. We can request a reduced fee via our partner team, but that requires 30–45 days lead time and additional approvals.
- Granularity: The console supports unit pricing down to 0.01 USD increments. You can model the price as "per 1M tokens" — there's no enforced token-unit, it's treated as a numeric unit.
- Billing flow: For Private Offers with monthly usage, the buyer is invoiced monthly for gross usage and the settlement to Redwood will be net after fees.

Requested from yours: please send the proposed gross -> net mapping given a 20% fee (we'll accept an additional column showing alternative 15%/25% scenarios). Also include the expected monthly commit band for the PO.

I attached the Marketplace PO guidance doc we referenced — it has a checklist for payment terms, minimum contract durations, and required PO fields.

Regards,
Tina Wong
Partner Programs, AWS Marketplace
tina.wong@amazon.com

Attachment: marketplace-po-guidance.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace PO: unit price mapping & target $/1M — follow-up

Thanks Tina — that helps a lot. Per your request, summarized below is the mapping we recommend based on Nimbus’s stated net target and the assumption of a 20% AWS fee. Attached is the same workbook with the formulas.

Assumptions (current):
- Expected monthly volume: 250M–450M tokens (input+output combined).
- Nimbus target (net to Redwood): $30–$45 per 1M tokens.
- Marketplace fee: 20% (AWS confirmed).

Recommended gross -> net mapping (per 1M tokens):
- Target net $30/1M -> Gross = $30 / (1 - 0.20) = $37.50/1M
- Target net $37/1M -> Gross = $37 / (1 - 0.20) = $46.25/1M
- Target net $45/1M -> Gross = $45 / (1 - 0.20) = $56.25/1M

Practical guidance:
- We recommend pricing the PO with the gross per-1M amounts rounded to the nearest $0.05 to avoid console rounding issues (e.g., $37.50, $46.25, $56.25 are fine).
- If Nimbus wants tiered volume pricing, we can set line items for ranges (e.g., 0–250M @ $56.25, 250–400M @ $46.25, 400M+ @ $37.50) and handle aggregation in Redwood’s billing reconciliation.
- If AWS can reduce fee to 15% via partner approvals, the gross would be lower (net $30 -> gross $35.29/1M). We included 15%/25% columns in the workbook for quick comparison.

Next actions we’ll take:
- Redwood will prepare a draft PO with both single-tier and a sample tiered mapping and circulate it to Nimbus and AWS for signoff.
- Nimbus to confirm preferred tier structure and final monthly commit band.
- Redwood finance/legal to review PO and confirm billing terms (net 30/PO acceptance, invoicing schedule).

Sam — can you confirm the 250–450M monthly band and whether you prefer the tiered approach? If you’re okay with the numbers above we’ll produce the PO draft and send it to Tina for acceptance workflow.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-scenario-0615.xlsx (revised with fee columns)
